description: Centralization risks analysis for Sapien PoQ v0.5 protocol - single points of failure, privilege concentration, and trust assumptions

single_admin_control.description: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holds unlimited power over protocol parameters, emergency controls, and upgrades
single_admin_control.impact_description: Complete rug pull possible via parameter changes, pause abuse, or malicious upgrades. Single key compromise = total protocol failure.
recommended_mitigations: Add timelocks (24-72 hours) for critical parameter changes
Separate emergency controls from parameter controls

role_management_monopoly.description: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can grant/revoke all roles including creating single points of failure
role_management_monopoly.impact_description: Admin can revoke legitimate operators, grant roles to malicious actors, or centralize all power
recommended_mitigations: Immutable role grants for critical functions

upgrade_authority_monopoly.description: UUPS upgrade mechanism controlled solely by DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE
upgrade_authority_monopoly.impact_description: Malicious upgrades can introduce backdoors, change economics, or steal funds

operator_discretion_monopoly.description: OPERATOR_ROLE makes subjective decisions on disputes and originator reports with no appeals
operator_discretion_monopoly.impact_description: Corrupt operators can steal escrows via fraudulent resolutions or protect malicious originators
recommended_mitigations: Implement jury systems for high-value disputes
Add evidence standards and review periods

keeper_dependency_centralization.description: Permissionless functions depend on keepers for execution (consensus, settlement, expiration)
keeper_dependency_centralization.impact_description: Censored keepers can prevent settlements, lock validator stakes, delay rewards

consensus_algorithm_centralization.description: Consensus algorithm centrally controlled despite pluggable architecture
consensus_algorithm_centralization.impact_description: Malicious consensus algorithm can manipulate all project outcomes

engine_contract_trust_monopoly.description: QualityEngine contract controls all stake operations via ENGINE_ROLE
engine_contract_trust_monopoly.impact_description: Contract compromise allows arbitrary slashing/unlocking of all user funds

erc4626_implementation_centralization.description: Single StakeVault contract holds all staked assets with known bypass vulnerabilities
erc4626_implementation_centralization.impact_description: STATIC-001 allows complete bypass of stake locks, destroying economic security

adapter_ecosystem_centralization.description: Token adapters can implement arbitrary logic in transferFrom calls
adapter_ecosystem_centralization.impact_description: Malicious adapters can censor users or manipulate token transfers

treasury_control_centralization.description: Treasury address centrally controlled, can be changed to attacker wallet
treasury_control_centralization.impact_description: Admin can redirect all future fee collection to malicious address

parameter_control_centralization.description: All economic parameters (fees, bonds, requirements) controlled by single admin
parameter_control_centralization.impact_description: Admin can set infinite fees, zero bonds, or manipulate economics to extract value

emergency_pause_centralization.description: Protocol-wide pause controlled by single admin with no user recourse
emergency_pause_centralization.impact_description: Admin can pause indefinitely, effectively rugging all users without withdrawal options

recommended_actions: Address all CRITICAL severity risks before deployment
Add community oversight for upgrades and parameters

operator_fairness.assumption: OPERATOR_ROLE resolves disputes fairly within time bounds

infrastructure_trust.assumption: ERC4337 stack operates correctly and doesn't censor
